boundary_rationale: The span opens the part on a reign-change notice, וַיִּ֨מְלָךְ מֶ֔לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בֶּן יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ תַּ֗חַת כָּנְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן יְה֣וֹיָקִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִמְלִ֛יךְ נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל בְּאֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.37.1, byte), matching “Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned as king instead of Coniah the son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah.” (web:Jer.37.1) — the bytes name the new king’s predecessor כָּנְיָ֨הוּ֙ (Konyahu, byte; oshb:Jer.37.1), the Coniah form, one of three name forms this king carries across the book (sweep: 3 verses); the reign is dated to a king “whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king” (web:Jer.37.1), the resh-family spelling נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר standing in the same clause (oshb:Jer.37.1, byte). Verse 2 continues the same notice with a general character report, וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֛ע ה֥וּא וַעֲבָדָ֖יו וְעַ֣ם הָאָ֑רֶץ אֶל דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִֽיא (oshb:Jer.37.2, byte), matching “But neither he, nor his servants, nor the people of the land, listened to Yahweh's words, which he spoke by the prophet Jeremiah.” (web:Jer.37.2) — naming the king, his servants, and the people of the land together, a summary claim about the reign rather than a dated scene. The inventory’s own setumah sits at oshb:Jer.36.32 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration under the Prophets addendum), immediately before this span’s own front seam; no mark falls inside verses 1-2 themselves.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding these two verses into the embassy scene that follows as one larger opening unit was rejected because verses 1-2 report the reign and its character with no named individual or dated moment, while verse 3 turns to a specific embassy sent by name.

boundary_rationale: A named embassy opens the scene, matching “Zedekiah the king sent Jehucal the son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah, the priest, to the prophet Jeremiah, saying, "Pray now to Yahweh our God for us."” (web:Jer.37.3) — Zedekiah sending two officials to ask Jeremiah to pray; a petuchah marks oshb:Jer.37.5 (single-witness WLC; Prophets tier-3, weak corroboration), texture on the notice that Pharaoh's army had left Egypt, וְחֵ֥יל פַּרְעֹ֖ה יָצָ֣א מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַיִּשְׁמְע֨וּ הַכַּשְׂדִּ֜ים הַצָּרִ֤ים עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ אֶת שִׁמְעָ֔ם וַיֵּ֣עָל֔וּ מֵעַ֖ל יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Jer.37.5, byte). The prophetic answer to that same embassy is framed by its own word-event notice, וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.37.6, byte), matching “Then Yahweh's word came to the prophet Jeremiah, saying,” (web:Jer.37.6), and opens with כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י (oshb:Jer.37.7, byte) — “Yahweh, the God of Israel, says” (web:Jer.37.7) — the divine formula, its mouth named as Yahweh answering the king's own messengers rather than any other speaker. A setumah closes the oracle's first turn at oshb:Jer.37.8 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration), וְשָׁ֨בוּ֙ הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וְנִלְחֲמ֖וּ עַל הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֑את וּלְכָדֻ֖הָ וּשְׂרָפֻ֥הָ בָאֵֽשׁ (oshb:Jer.37.8, byte), before the reply continues through the Chaldeans' certain return in verses 9-10.

boundary_rationale: The scene turns to Jeremiah's own movement once the siege lifts, וְהָיָ֗ה בְּהֵֽעָלוֹת֙ חֵ֣יל הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים מֵעַ֖ל יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם מִפְּנֵ֖י חֵ֥יל פַּרְעֹֽה (oshb:Jer.37.11, byte), matching “When the army of the Chaldeans had withdrawn from Jerusalem for fear of Pharaoh's army,” (web:Jer.37.11); a setumah marks this same verse in the inventory (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration), texture at the turn rather than its warrant. A petuchah closes the span at oshb:Jer.37.16 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration), כִּ֣י בָ֧א יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ אֶל בֵּ֥ית הַבּ֖וֹר וְאֶל הַֽחֲנֻ֑יוֹת וַיֵּֽשֶׁב שָׁ֥ם יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים (oshb:Jer.37.16, byte), where Jeremiah is reported to have remained many days.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the seizure at the gate from the imprisonment that follows into two rows was rejected because no formula, addressee change, or dated notice interrupts the single chain from seizure to the many days in the cells.

boundary_rationale: A petuchah closes the preceding span at oshb:Jer.37.16 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration) immediately before a fresh royal action opens this one, וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֜הוּ וַיִּקָּחֵ֗הוּ (oshb:Jer.37.17, byte), matching “then Zedekiah the king sent and had him brought out. A setumah also marks this same verse, oshb:Jer.37.17 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration under the Prophets addendum). Jeremiah's own plea follows, matching “Now please hear, my lord the king: please let my supplication be presented before you, that you not cause me to return to the house of Jonathan the scribe, lest I die there."” (web:Jer.37.20) — addressed to the king with אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.37.20, byte), the human “my lord” used of a king rather than the distinct divine-title pointing of the same three consonants, asking not to be returned to Jonathan's house. The king answers by committing him instead to the court of the guard, matching “Then Zedekiah the king commanded, and they committed Jeremiah into the court of the guard. boundary_rationale: A new set of four named officials opens the span, וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע שְׁפַטְיָ֣ה בֶן מַתָּ֗ן וּגְדַלְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן פַּשְׁח֔וּר וְיוּכַל֙ בֶּן שֶׁ֣לֶמְיָ֔הוּ וּפַשְׁח֖וּר בֶּן מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה אֶ֨ת הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ מְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל כָּל הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte), matching “Shephatiah the son of Mattan, Gedaliah the son of Pashhur, Jucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur the son of Malchijah heard the words that Jeremiah spoke to all the people, saying,” (web:Jer.38.1); a setumah marks this same verse, oshb:Jer.38.1 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration). What they heard is Jeremiah's own proclamation to the people, opening הַיֹּשֵׁב֙ בָּעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את יָמ֕וּת בַּחֶ֖רֶב בָּרָעָ֣ב וּבַדָּ֑בֶר (oshb:Jer.38.2, byte; a ketiv/qere note also sits later in this verse, not engaged by this splice) — matching “He who remains in this city will die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence,” (web:Jer.38.2) — the divine formula naming Yahweh as its mouth; a further setumah falls at this same verse, oshb:Jer.38.2. The officials petition the king that Jeremiah be put to death for weakening the soldiers' resolve, matching “Then the princes said to the king, "Please let this man be put to death, because he weakens the hands of the men of war who remain in this city, and the hands of all the people, in speaking such words to them; for this man doesn't seek the welfare of this people, but harm."” (web:Jer.38.4); Zedekiah answers that he is in their hand, matching “Zedekiah the king said, "Behold, he is in your hand; for the king can't do anything to oppose you."” (web:Jer.38.5), and they cast him into Malchijah's cistern, וַיִּקְח֣וּ אֶֽת יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ וַיַּשְׁלִ֨כוּ אֹת֜וֹ אֶל הַבּ֣וֹר מַלְכִּיָּ֣הוּ בֶן הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר֙ בַּחֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָ֔ה וַיְשַׁלְּח֥וּ אֶֽת יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בַּחֲבָלִ֑ים וּבַבּ֤וֹר אֵֽין מַ֨יִם֙ כִּ֣י אִם טִ֔יט וַיִּטְבַּ֥ע יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בַּטִּֽיט (oshb:Jer.38.6, byte), where a third setumah closes the span at this same verse, oshb:Jer.38.6 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration).

boundary_rationale: Ebedmelech the Ethiopian opens a rescue scene once the setumah closing the preceding span at oshb:Jer.38.6 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration) gives way to וַיִּשְׁמַ֡ע עֶֽבֶד מֶ֨לֶךְ הַכּוּשִׁ֜י אִ֣ישׁ סָרִ֗יס וְהוּא֙ בְּבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּֽי נָתְנ֥וּ אֶֽת יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ אֶל הַבּ֑וֹר וְהַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּשַׁ֥עַר בִּנְיָמִֽן (oshb:Jer.38.7, byte), matching “Now when Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, a eunuch, who was in the king's house, heard that they had put Jeremiah in the dungeon (the king was then sitting in Benjamin's gate),” (web:Jer.38.7). He is likely to die in the place where he is, because of the famine; for there is no more bread in the city."” (web:Jer.38.9) — opening אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.38.9, byte), the same human vocative used of Zedekiah earlier in these chapters rather than a divine title — and the king commands the rescue, וַיְצַוֶּ֣ה הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֛ת עֶֽבֶד מֶ֥לֶךְ הַכּוּשִׁ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר קַ֣ח בְּיָדְךָ֤ מִזֶּה֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְֽהַעֲלִ֜יתָ אֶֽת יִרְמְיָ֧הוּ הַנָּבִ֛יא מִן הַבּ֖וֹר בְּטֶ֥רֶם יָמֽוּת (oshb:Jer.38.10, byte). boundary_rationale: Jeremiah turns from direct counsel to a further disclosure, וְאִם מָאֵ֥ן אַתָּ֖ה לָצֵ֑את זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִרְאַ֖נִי יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.38.21, byte), matching “But if you refuse to go out, this is the word that Yahweh has shown me:” (web:Jer.38.21) — a showing-formula distinct from the spoken oracle just closed. The span closes on the execution of that sentence, matching “Moreover he put out Zedekiah's eyes and bound him in fetters, to carry him to Babylon.” (web:Jer.39.7) — the king's sons killed before his eyes and his own eyes put out, before the account turns to the city's fate.
